You are helping a user write SQL queries to a database. If something is not clear, you can ask the user to clarify what they need. The schema for the database being accessed is the following:
        
CREATE TABLE museum (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Num_of_Staff INT,
    Open_Year TEXT,
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visitor (
    ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Name TEXT,
    Level_of_membership INT,
    Age INT,
    UNIQUE (ID)
);

CREATE TABLE visit (
    Museum_ID INT   PRIMARY KEY,
    visitor_ID TEXT   PRIMARY KEY,
    Num_of_Ticket INT,
    Total_spent REAL,
    PRIMARY KEY (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    UNIQUE (Museum_ID, visitor_ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (visitor_ID) REFERENCES visitor(ID),
    FOREIGN KEY (Museum_ID) REFERENCES museum(Museum_ID)
);

To get **frequent museum visitors**, we need a definition of “frequent”. Common options:

- visited **at least N times** (across all museums)
- visited **at least N distinct museums**
- visitors with the **most visits** (top K)

Here are the SQL patterns:

### 1) Visitors who made at least N visits (set N = 5 here)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS visit_count
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY visit_count DESC;
```

### 2) Visitors who visited at least N distinct museums (set N = 3 here)
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) >= 3
ORDER BY museums_visited DESC;
```

### 3) Top 10 most frequent visitors
```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(*) AS visit_count
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
ORDER BY visit_count DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

Which definition do you want (at least N visits, distinct museums, or top K), and what should N/K be?
I want to consider people who visited multiple museums.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) > 1
ORDER BY museums_visited DESC, v.Name;
```
I want to look at visitors who have been to more than one museum.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) > 1
ORDER BY museums_visited DESC, v.Name;
```
I want to look for the unique ID of these visitors too.

You can include the unique visitor ID (from `visitor.ID`) like this:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID AS visitor_id,
  v.Name,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor AS v
JOIN visit AS vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) > 1
ORDER BY museums_visited DESC, v.ID;
```
and I want to grab the names of these visitors too.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) > 1
ORDER BY v.ID;
```
I also want to take a look at the visitors' ages along with those details.

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age  AS visitor_age,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Age
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) > 1
ORDER BY museums_visited DESC, v.ID;
```
Just to clarify, I want to focus on visitors specifically going to museums.

If you mean “only visitors who have at least one museum visit recorded” (and among them, those who visited more than one museum), the query below already does that because it joins to `visit`:

```sql
SELECT
  v.ID   AS visitor_id,
  v.Name AS visitor_name,
  v.Age  AS visitor_age,
  COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) AS museums_visited
FROM visitor v
JOIN visit vi
  ON vi.visitor_ID = v.ID
GROUP BY v.ID, v.Name, v.Age
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT vi.Museum_ID) > 1
ORDER BY museums_visited DESC, v.ID;
```

If instead you want to restrict to a *particular* museum (or museum name), tell me which one and I’ll adjust it.
